<text>
# Summary of UK Political Manifesto 2017

## Overview and Brexit Position

The manifesto presents a vision for an independent Britain outside the European Union. It establishes six "Brexit tests" that must be met: legal supremacy (freedom from European court jurisdiction), migration control, maritime sovereignty (200-mile exclusive economic zone), trade independence, financial separation, and completion before 2020.

The document argues Britain should have left the EU by repealing the European Communities Act directly, rather than following Article 50, which it characterizes as designed to obstruct departure. It criticizes the negotiating approach as too accommodating to European interests.

## Economic Policies

### Taxation and Finance
The manifesto proposes raising the income tax personal allowance to £13,500 and the higher rate threshold to £55,000. Inheritance tax thresholds would increase to £500,000 per individual. Business rates would be cut by 20% for premises valued under £50,000.

VAT would be removed from domestic energy bills and hot takeaway food. The television licence would be phased out over three years. Insurance Premium Tax would be frozen.

The document criticizes multinational corporations avoiding taxation and pledges stricter enforcement.

### Funding Sources
Approximately £35 billion in savings would come from:
- Reducing overseas aid from 0.7% to 0.2% of gross national income
- Cancelling the HS2 rail project
- Replacing the Barnett Formula with needs-based allocation
- Ending EU budget contributions

## Fishing and Maritime

The manifesto emphasizes restoring British fishing rights, claiming the industry could be worth £6.3 billion annually. It proposes repealing the 1964 London Convention on Fishing, creating a dedicated Fisheries Protection Force, and requiring all fish caught in British waters to be landed and sold domestically. Time-limited licenses would be available for foreign vessels while the domestic industry rebuilds.

## Housing

A Housing Development Corporation would be established to acquire primarily brownfield sites and construct factory-built modular homes. These would be sold to first-time buyers under 40 with 10% deposits, targeting prices under £100,000 for two-bedroom houses. The scheme aims to deliver 100,000 additional affordable homes annually.

Restrictions would prevent these homes being used for private rental or sold on the open market—owners must sell back to the Corporation. The manifesto also proposes reviewing housing associations' operations.

## Healthcare

NHS funding would increase by £9 billion annually by 2021/22, with an additional £2 billion for social care. Medical school training places would rise from 7,500 to 10,000, with tuition fees covered for graduates committing to NHS work. Nursing bursaries would be reinstated.

Only British citizens or foreign nationals with five consecutive years of tax contributions would access non-urgent NHS care. Others must maintain comprehensive medical insurance. The manifesto proposes establishing a Department for Health and Care to integrate the NHS and social care systems.

Mental health spending would increase by £500 million annually, with maximum waiting times reduced to 28 days. School-based counselling would expand.

## Immigration and Integration

The manifesto proposes reducing net migration to zero over five years through a points-based system applying equally to all nationalities except Irish citizens. A five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration would follow EU departure.

New migrants would wait five years before accessing benefits or non-urgent healthcare. Work visas would prioritize those earning minimum £30,000 annually with employer sponsorship.

The document calls for disbanding sharia councils, banning face coverings in public, and establishing "one law for all." It proposes criminalizing failure to report female genital mutilation, with annual screening for at-risk girls and increased sentencing.

Integration measures include testing social attitudes of migration applicants and requiring Ofsted inspections when concerns arise about unequal treatment or extremist views in schools.

## Education

Grammar schools would be expanded to one per town, with transfer examinations available up to age 16. Vocational training modeled on Germany's dual system would combine classroom learning with workplace experience.

Tuition fees would be abolished for science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine students who subsequently work in Britain for five years. Maintenance grants would be restored. Funding would cease for courses where fewer than two-thirds of graduates find graduate-level employment within five years.

## Defense and Veterans

Defense spending would reach a "genuine" 2% of GDP plus £1 billion additional annually. Armed forces personnel would increase by 20,000. The manifesto criticizes recent reductions leaving the Army at its smallest since Napoleonic times.

A Veterans' Administration would provide centralized support services. Homeless veterans would receive hostels and priority housing allocation. Ex-service personnel with 12 years' service would be guaranteed jobs in police, prison, or border services.

## Policing and Justice

The manifesto proposes 20,000 additional police officers, 7,000 prison officers, and 4,000 border force staff. Stop and search powers would be reinstated fully. Foreign criminals would serve sentences in their countries of origin where possible.

The European Arrest Warrant would be rejected. Labour's Human Rights legislation would be repealed, and Britain would withdraw from the European Court of Human Rights, replaced by a domestic Bill of Rights.

## Elderly Care and Disability

The pension "triple lock" would be maintained, increasing payments by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. All pensioner benefits would continue without means testing. Women could opt for flexible retirement from age 60 with adjusted pension levels.

Social care funding would increase by £2 billion annually. Work capability assessments for disabled people would be reformed following consultation.

## Transport

HS2 would be cancelled, with funds redirected to upgrading existing rail services and improving east-west northern connections. Road tolls on public roads would be eliminated. The third Heathrow runway is opposed.

Regional airport expansion would be supported, including Manston Airport in Kent. Electric vehicle charging infrastructure would be expanded, while diesel drivers would be protected from punitive taxes given previous government encouragement of diesel purchases.

## Constitutional Reform

The House of Lords would be abolished. An English Parliament of 375 members would be established with its own First Minister. The House of Commons would be reduced to 325 members elected proportionally. These changes would reduce total legislators from 1,475 to 700.

Binding local referenda would be held on major local issues. A citizen's initiative would allow national referenda on petitions gaining sufficient signatures.

## Energy and Environment

The 2008 Climate Change Act would be repealed. A diverse energy mix including coal, nuclear, shale gas, and renewables would be supported. Britain would withdraw from the Paris climate agreement. Green levies on energy bills would be removed.

Ancient woodlands would receive enhanced protection. Fracking would be prohibited in national parks. A deposit scheme for plastic bottles would be investigated.

## Animal Welfare

Live animal exports for slaughter would be banned. CCTV would be required in all abattoirs. Meat labeling would identify slaughter methods. Maximum sentences for animal cruelty would triple.

## Foreign Affairs

Traditional alliances through NATO, the UN Security Council, and the Commonwealth would be maintained. A free trade agreement with the EU would be pursued, but trading on World Trade Organization terms is presented as acceptable if negotiations fail.

The overseas aid budget reduction would fund a naval hospital ship for humanitarian missions and supporting armed forces operations.
